title: Small families of subsets: pseudointersections, maximality, and ultrafilter bases
summary: Three uncountable minima measure failures of pseudointersections, extensions of almost disjoint families, and small ultrafilter bases.
abstract: An infinite approximate intersection of a family of sets is contained in each member apart from finitely many exceptions. Every countable family of infinite subsets of the natural numbers has one if all finite intersections are infinite; the pseudointersection number measures the smallest family size for which this can fail. Two related numbers measure the smallest size of an infinite maximal family of infinite sets with finite pairwise intersections, and the smallest size of a base for an ultrafilter containing no finite sets. Such a base consists of members of the ultrafilter and supplies a subset of every member. All three numbers are uncountable and at most the size of the real line, and the pseudointersection number is no larger than the ultrafilter number.

based_on.title: Combinatorial Cardinal Characteristics of the Continuum
based_on.pages: 37 (Definition 6.16 and Remark 6.17), 39–40 (6.22–6.23), 51–52 (8.1–8.4), 56–58 (9.1, 9.6); author draft dated November 24, 2003; direct pseudointersection comparisons supplied locally
